newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products surge on Iraq sale delay.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products surge on Iraq sale delay.

text.p: Singapore oil products rose sharply on crude gains following news that the United Nations (U.N.) had delayed limited oil sales by Iraq, traders said on Monday.

Gas oil chalked up an impressive 70 cents gain on the back of an almost similar rise to Brent crude. Traders said the rise was largely due to the higher screen values with no change to the fundamentals seen. September gas oil paper traded to a high of $26.60 and closed at around this level at $25.55-25.65. Bid by a trader for a 150,000 barrel lifting in end September at $26.50 failed to attract any selling interest.

Jet prices were also firmer despite high regional stocks. Traders said price hikes was mainly due to the higher crude values. India bought 25,000 tonnes aviation turbine fuel at a premium of $2.30 per barrel over the MidEast spot quotes, on a cost-and-freight basis. Crude hikes also boosted Singapore naphtha to its highest level in at least two years but high levels stymied any trade on paper or physical. September paper was bid as firm as $20.45, a 55 cent leap from Friday. Gasoline was more actively talked with 95-octane unleaded cargoes lifting September 18-22 bid as high as $23.00, 95-octane traded on Friday at $22.50.
A Thai refiner was offering an early September 250,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded at about 25 cents below Singapore quotes fob Sri Racha.

High sulphur fuel oil prices moved up by $3 per tonne from Friday's indications. Sentiment is cautious, said a trader. There may be enough oil around, but prices are up on the back of the Iraq news, he said. While demand from China remained thin, traders noted that Indian demand has improved. Low stocks and the onset of winter demand is expected to prompt India to buy up to 100,000 tonnes of fuel oil per month until February, traders said. --Singapore Newsroom (+65-8703093)
